resources.string:
This app reads vehicle telemetry such as speed, gear, EV battery state, pedal position, and turn signals.

It never writes to any vehicle property.

Data leaves the car only over a local network connection to your Raspberry Pi driver display.
Live property data is hidden while the vehicle is in motion.\n\nShift to Park (P) or apply the parking brake to view.
Notifies you that the EX30 Companion is forwarding vehicle telemetry to your Raspberry Pi driver display.
Forwarding vehicle telemetry to Pi driver display
Save the Pi network in car settings once for automatic reconnection. Leave the name empty to use the Wi-Fi network selected in car settings.
Use up to 32 UTF-8 bytes for the network name.
Could not save the Wi-Fi password on this device.
Enter the Pi host, then tap Connect.
Wi-Fi unavailable. Check the network and tap Connect to retry.
Wi-Fi is off. Tap Connect to turn it on.
Open Wi-Fi and enter the password again.
Android could not save the network. Check the Wi-Fi name and password in car settings.
Join the Pi network in car Wi-Fi settings and enable auto-connect.
Tap Connect to allow the bridge to check the Wi-Fi name in the background.

Android requires location access to read the Wi-Fi name, including after the car starts. Companion checks this name before sending data to the Pi. In Permissions → Location, choose “%1$s” and enable precise location.
Check Location and the Companion location permission in car settings.
Location is off. Tap Connect to enable Wi-Fi name checks.
Android hid the Wi-Fi name. Check Location and the Companion location permission.
Open Wi-Fi in car settings, then return and tap Connect.
